HC-MoE v14.1: Out of Domain, at the Last MoE Layer

The confirmatory run on two benchmarks the series had never used — and what it does to the scope of the Qwen claim
October 11, 2026 · v14.1
Revision note (v14.1). Every routing p-value, null fit and HC value in this series comes from the last MoE layer of each large model. Earlier reports never said so; this revision states it in the setup, scopes the findings to it, and fixes three passages that implied otherwise. No number changes. Abstract. v13 asked for the one test the series had never run: the full pipeline on text it had never looked at, with the prediction written down first. Two benchmarks were chosen, mbpp (Python code) and dialogsum (dialogue summaries). The prediction was that Qwen's association would be positive and outside the floor under both difficulty controls within token strings, and that Gemma's would be negative or null. The result is mixed, and it narrows what the series can claim. On dialogsum, Qwen meets the prediction by the letter: within strings, r(HC, IG | CEsmall) = +0.012 and | CEbig = +0.100, both outside the floor implied by the bootstrap. The margin is thin: +0.012 against a floor of 0.0067 that had to be inferred, because the drop has no measured effective sample size, and it would fail against the main study's 0.0128. On mbpp the scale-specific part goes the other way (-0.028, 8 of 10 configurations negative). And on both new benchmarks Qwen's raw correlation with IG is negative (-0.043 and -0.035), where it was positive in all nine studied benchmarks. The pre-registered rule is met by the letter, through dialogsum. I do not read that as confirmation: Qwen's ‘where scale helps’ is now a tier-A finding on the nine studied benchmarks, and its reach beyond them is unsettled. Gemma's raw inversion does carry over (negative on both), but its within-string scale-specific part is positive on dialogsum. This report also corrects how v11–v13 described the sign-agreement criterion. The criterion they applied was the tier-B consistency score (at least 9 of 10 configurations), not the ‘70% of configurations’ their text said; no verdict changes.

1. Research goals and where the study stands

The two primary questions

  1. Does HC track token difficulty? r(HC, CEbig) and r(HC, CEsmall), answered first.
  2. Does HC track Intelligence Gain beyond difficulty? r(HC, IG), IG = CEsmall − CEbig, under controls for either model's loss, within token strings — and, from this report, on text outside the studied benchmarks.

Null estimator, HC variant, control, statistic, correlation measure, shape, token identity and domain are secondary axes: checks on those two answers, not findings of their own.

What this drop changes

The confirmatory run meets its rule by the letter, and narrows the claim anyway

Confirmatory run on unseen benchmarks (P0). Rule written in v13: if Qwen is positive and outside the floor under both controls within strings on a new benchmark, the claim is confirmed out of domain; if it is inside the floor on all of them, the claim is restated as holding on the studied benchmarks only. Met by the letter on dialogsum. But the rule did not anticipate a benchmark going significantly the other way, and mbpp does. Taking the run as a whole — one narrow pass, one reversal, and a raw correlation negative on both — the honest reading is that the claim is established on the studied benchmarks and unsettled outside them.

The experiment's summary labels Qwen/dialogsum ‘FAIL_OUT_OF_DOMAIN’, apparently against a fixed floor near the main study's 0.0128. The series grades each cell at its own effective sample size; dialogsum's, implied by its bootstrap CI widths, is about 85,010, giving a floor of 0.0067. Against the main-study floor, dialogsum's value falls short by 0.0005. Measuring dialogsum's ESS directly settles it.

Not run: the shared-expert ablation, the Qwen3-8B partner and lambada's top tokens under every null. They are carried forward.

Revision v14.1: every result is about the last MoE layer

All routing p-values, the five null estimators' fits and the HC values come from one place: the router of the last MoE layer of each large model — 128 routed experts in Qwen3-30B-A3B and gemma-4-26B-A4B, 64 in ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B, 32 in LFM2-8B-A1B. No other layer was measured. This was true of every drop; the reports should have said so from the start, and it is now in section 2.

What it changes. Scope, not numbers. Every finding below is a statement about last-layer routing. ‘Qwen's HC marks the tokens where scale helps’ means the last MoE layer's routing does; whether earlier layers do the same is untested. Three passages are corrected: the GLM description (‘each layer’), the token section's note that its routing statistics came ‘from one layer’ (they come from the same layer as all HC), and the shared-expert ablation design in section 25, which becomes simpler.

Why it matters for interpretation. The last MoE layer is the one closest to the output head, so its routing is the most directly tied to the next-token prediction the losses measure. That makes the difficulty correlations less surprising and raises a question the series has not asked: does HC add anything beyond simpler last-layer signals, such as router entropy or the hidden state's norm? Section 25 adds that test. It also gives back, honestly, the question the retired Q-slices pretended to answer: where in the network the relationship lives. A per-layer sweep is proposed. Finally, HC's resolution depends on how many experts the layer has, which may be part of why Liquid (32) and ERNIE (64) show no family-level effect; that is a hypothesis.

Main findings so far

What the project holds after this report. Nothing studied before is withdrawn; what changes is scope, twice over. Every result is a statement about the routing of each large model's last MoE layer (v14.1). And every Qwen result was established on nine benchmarks; the first two outside them do not reproduce its raw sign.

2. Nomenclature and setup

TermDefinition
Big CE / Small CECross-entropy of the large / small model on the same token
Intelligence Gain (IG)IG = CEsmall − CEbig. Positive means the large model wins.
Where it is measuredThe last MoE layer of each large model, only. Router logits from that layer give the per-expert routing p-values; the null estimators are fitted to that layer's logits; HC is computed from them. The small models enter only through their loss.
HC (max_20pct)Higher Criticism over the token's per-expert routing p-values in the last MoE layer, maximised over the top 20% of that layer's experts.
Primary gridFull token set × 5 null estimators (GMM, JohnsonSU, KDE, StudentT, StudentTSkewed) × 2 variants = 10 configurations per cell, 36 cells, 360 configurations. The Lindsey GLM is out (v9 Laplace, v10 Gaussian).
Spearman / winsorisedRank correlation; Pearson after clipping each variable at its 1st and 99th (or 0.5th and 99.5th) percentiles. Same passage bootstrap as the raw values.
Rank ratioSpearman / Pearson for a cell. Below 0.5 demotes a tier-A cell (pre-registered in v8).
HC ventile, top-quartile share20 equal-count HC bins; the share of the HC–IG covariance contributed by tokens above HC's 75th percentile (about 46% for a linear relationship).
Q50–Q95Tokens with IG at or above its Nth percentile. Retired as evidence in v8.
control = fisher / pminPartial correlation on the dense Fisher combination / on the strongest expert's p-value.
ESS, deflationEffective sample size from within-passage autocorrelation; nominal n / ESS.

v9: GLM's Laplace tail compresses HC on the most anomalous tokens

The Lindsey GLM in empirical_null_lindsey.py fits a Poisson GLM to histogram counts in the centre of the last MoE layer's logit distribution, with a design linear in |x − μ| — a Laplace shape. Extrapolated into the tail it decays exponentially where a Gaussian decays quadratically in the exponent; on Gemma's layer a logit of 4.0 gets p = 0.0117 under GLM and 9.8×10−9 under GMM. Dropping it brought the estimator spread from 0.0252 to 0.0134, kept every tier-A cell and every family sign, and became the primary grid.

Figure 3 — Mean IG correlation under each null estimator, Laplace GLM included (mandatory figure)

Pooled over families, so each bar sits inside the floor through cancellation. GLM, in grey, is the low outlier; the other five span 0.0134.

v10: Gaussian decay removes the offset and replaces it with scatter

The same Lindsey fit with a quadratic design (type='gaussian') was run on all 36 cells. On family means it looks repaired in three families: offsets of -0.0045 (Qwen), +0.0076 (Gemma) and -0.0013 (Liquid), against Laplace's -0.0302, -0.0259 and -0.0044. In ERNIE it is worse than Laplace (-0.0266 against -0.0183).

Cell by cell it does not behave like the other five. It lands inside their range in 39% of cells (13 below, 9 above). To read that number: if it were interchangeable with them, it would land inside the range of five about 4 times in 6 (67%); each of the five, checked against the other four, lands inside 50%–72% of the time, close to the 60% expected for four. Laplace GLM, for comparison, was inside 50%: biased, but less erratic. GLM-Gaussian also reverses the sign in 5 cells where the five agree beyond the noise floor (ERNIE/structured-wikipedia, Gemma/tinystories, Liquid/mmlu, Qwen/hellaswag, Qwen/tinystories), and it sits outside the range in 5 of the 13 tier-A cells.

The pre-registered rule says drop the Lindsey GLM permanently, and that is now the design. The reason differs between the two tail shapes: Laplace shifted every cell the same way; Gaussian moves cells in both directions by up to 0.065.

Figure 4 — How often each estimator lands inside the range of the others

Green: each of the five against the other four (60% expected if interchangeable). Grey and amber: the two GLM versions against all five (67% expected). Standard variant.

Figure 5 — Mean offset from the five-estimator mean, by family

Gaussian decay fixes the offset in Qwen, Gemma and Liquid and makes ERNIE worse. The scatter behind these means is in the previous figure.

Figure 6 — Estimator spread by family on the primary grid

Floor 0.0128. Gemma is the only family still clearly above it, and less so on ranks.

What is and is not established about why. The experiment shows that GLM-Gaussian scatters; it does not show the cause. Its summary attributes it to the Lindsey method's sensitivity to histogram binning and to heavy kurtosis in routing logits. Binning sensitivity is plausible — the fit uses 71 bins over the central 5–95% of the layer's logits — but was not varied, and kurtosis was not measured. Note also that the experiment compares on the standard variant only, so its family means differ slightly from the two-variant means elsewhere in this report. Five methods agreeing does not prove them right; it shows the answer does not hinge on which of them is used.

Gemma, per benchmark. The five estimators agree on sign in 9 of 9 benchmarks and differ by 0.017–0.050 within a benchmark, mostly GMM (least negative) against StudentTSkewed (most negative). Gemma's inversion is estimator-robust; its size is uncertain by up to a factor of about two.

The tier-A list is not an outlier artifact

Clipping each variable at its 1st and 99th percentiles leaves every tier-A correlation within 0.91–1.05× of its raw value, and clipping at 0.5% gives the same picture. If a few extreme tokens were carrying the Pearson values, clipping them would have collapsed those cells. It does not touch them. The concern that has sat in this series' ‘not run’ column since v1 is closed in that form.

Ranks are harsher. Of the 14 Pearson tier-A cells on the primary grid, 11 are also tier A on Spearman. Under the pre-registered rule, only one falls below half: ERNIE/fineweb-edu, r = +0.0324 but Spearman +0.0006, which goes to B. It is the cell the GLM drop had just promoted, so the two rules leave the tier-A list exactly where v8 had it. Two more are flagged rank-sensitive — tier A on Pearson and under the rule, tier B on ranks: Gemma/competition_math (ratio 0.74), Liquid/tinystories (ratio 0.78).

Figure 8 — Pearson against Spearman, all 36 cells

Dashed grey: Spearman equals Pearson. Dotted amber: Spearman is half of Pearson, the rule's line. Gemma (green) and Liquid (purple) sit on the diagonal; Qwen (blue) falls toward the half line.

Figure 9 — The Pearson tier-A cells under three correlation measures

Winsorised (grey) tracks Pearson in every cell. Spearman (amber) mostly does too. The exceptions: ERNIE/fineweb-edu, where it collapses to zero; Qwen/fineweb-edu, where it roughly halves; and Gemma/competition_math and Liquid/tinystories, which lose about a quarter.

Gemma's association is as strong on ranks; Qwen's is not

Across cells with |r| > 0.03, the median Spearman/Pearson ratio is 0.93 in Gemma, 0.92 in Liquid, 0.81 in ERNIE and 0.71 in Qwen. Gemma's negative association is beyond the floor in 8 of 9 benchmarks on Pearson and 8 of 9 on ranks; in structured-wikipedia and tinystories it is stronger on ranks. Qwen's positive association clears the floor in 8 of 9 benchmarks on Pearson and 4 on ranks: in hellaswag, pg19, structured-wikipedia, tinystories the rank correlation is near zero, and none is significantly negative.

Winsorising leaves those Qwen cells intact, so the difference is not a few extreme tokens. The most likely reading is a relationship that is flat through most of HC's range and rises in its upper part: Pearson weights that part by its magnitude, ranks do not. Two v8 observations fit the same shape — Qwen's empirical top-decile lift is 1.5× what a linear relationship predicts, and selecting on high IG inflated r rather than shrinking it.

v10 update: the binned curves in section 6 test this reading and only partly bear it out. Tail concentration is real in competition_math and lambada, but it does not predict which cells lose strength on ranks, and ties are ruled out. The rank gap in Qwen's weaker benchmarks remains unexplained.

Gemma's mean is the same on ranks. Qwen's drops by about a third.

They keep tier A here, as the rule's letter requires, and carry a rank-sensitive flag in every table. A reader who prefers the Spearman tier throughout gets 12 tier-A cells instead of 13.

6. The shape of the HC–IG relationship

78%
competition_math covariance in HC's top quartile
0.74 → 1.63
lambada mean IG, 75th pct → top 5% of HC
3 up / 2 down
Qwen benchmarks with a top-bin jump beyond the bands
53%
Gemma median top-quartile share (linear ≈ 46%)

For every cell, tokens were sorted by HC into 20 equal-count bins (ventiles) and mean IG was computed per bin with bootstrap bands. The covariance was split by HC quartile, and r computed separately above and below HC's 75th percentile. All on one configuration (GMM, standard), the same one experiment 3 used. A reference point for the covariance split: if IG rose linearly with a normally distributed HC, the top quartile would already carry about 46% of the covariance, because those tokens sit furthest from the mean. The rule's 70% is well above that.

In Qwen's strongest benchmarks, the large model's advantage surges among the most anomalous tokens

competition_math is the clearest case. Across the lowest 75% of HC, mean IG barely moves (0.08 in the bottom ventile, 0.20 at the 75th percentile) and the correlation there is +0.010, inside the floor. Then it jumps: 1.59 and 1.20 in the top two ventiles, far outside the bands. The top quartile carries 78% of the covariance. This is the one tier-A cell that meets the pre-registered threshold condition.

lambada has the same surge on a rising body: IG climbs from 0.38 to 0.74 across the lower 75% (r = +0.046, outside the floor), then reaches 1.40 and 1.63. 77% of the covariance is in the top quartile, but the body is correlated, so the threshold condition is not met. structured-wikipedia (tier B) looks similar.

In both cells the top 10% of HC is where the large model wins by the most. In practical terms, HC above its 90th percentile picks out 8,419 tokens in competition_math with mean IG 1.39 against 0.15 for the rest (9×), and 4,007 in lambada with 1.51 against 0.68 (2.2×).

Figure 11 — Qwen: mean IG across HC ventiles, four benchmarks

Each curve is centred on its own mean so shapes can be compared. Blue and teal surge in the top two ventiles; amber and red rise across the body and fall at the top. GMM, standard.

It is not Qwen's general shape, and it does not explain the rank gap

In fineweb-edu and pg19 the curve goes the other way at the top: IG rises through the body and then falls in the top ventile (1.08 → 0.80 and 1.36 → 0.69, beyond the bands). In race the top is flat. fineweb-edu and race are tier A, and their correlation lives in the body (top-quartile shares 38% and 45%, below the linear reference). So the threshold condition holds in one of Qwen's four tier-A cells, and the pre-registered rule's verdict for Qwen as a whole is that neither branch applies: the Pearson grades stand, and HC-thresholding does not become the default analysis.

v9 proposed tail concentration as the reason Qwen loses strength on ranks. The data do not support it. competition_math, the most concentrated cell, has a Spearman/Pearson ratio of 1.00; fineweb-edu, body-driven, has 0.66. Across the 22 cells with |r| > 0.03, ρ(top-quartile share, rank ratio) = -0.36 (p = 0.10). Ties are ruled out as well: HC has many repeated values, but the largest single block is a median 0.19% of tokens (at most 4.4%), and Gemma, with more ties than Qwen, loses nothing on ranks. Why Qwen's weaker benchmarks fade on ranks is still open.

Gemma's inversion is linear through the bulk

Gemma's top quartile carries a median 53% of the covariance, about what a straight line gives. In its four tier-A cells the correlation is negative below HC's 75th percentile and negative or near zero above it. The binned curves are close to straight lines (binned R² up to 0.80 in pg19). Anomalous routing in Gemma marks easier-than-expected tokens for the large model across HC's whole range, not in a tail.

Figure 12 — Gemma: mean IG across HC ventiles, its four tier-A benchmarks

Steady declines, no tail feature. Same scale conventions as the Qwen figure.

Figure 13 — Share of the HC–IG covariance in HC's top quartile, the 13 tier-A cells

About 46% is what a linear relationship gives; the rule's threshold is 70%. Only Qwen's competition_math and lambada clear 70%. Bars coloured by family (Qwen blue, ERNIE red, Gemma green, Liquid purple).

How far this goes. One null configuration, so the shapes inherit GMM's calibration. Correlations within a quartile are attenuated by the restricted HC range, so the covariance shares are the better comparison. Shares are meaningless where the total covariance is near zero: 10 cells have shares below 0 or above 1 for that reason, 0 of them tier A. The surges in competition_math and lambada involve the top 10% of tokens, roughly 4,000–8,000 per cell, so they are well measured, but they have not yet been checked against token difficulty.

The shape across compute ratios

The Qwen compute-ratio partners were binned the same way for lambada and competition_math. In lambada, the rise across the body of HC (bin 1 to the 75th percentile) falls from 0.36 with the 0.6B partner to 0.27 with 1.7B and 0.05 with 4B, while the jump into the top ventile goes 0.89 → 0.43 → 0.34. With the 4B partner almost nothing is left in the body; what remains is among the most anomalous tokens. In competition_math the top-ventile jump grows with the 1.7B partner (1.01 → 1.27) before halving with 4B (0.55). The experiment's own summary reads this as the partner ‘selectively compressing the tail’. In lambada the curves say the opposite: the body goes first.

Figure 14 — Qwen lambada: mean IG across HC ventiles for the three small partners

Large model and HC fixed; only the small partner changes. With 4B (amber) the body is nearly flat and the top ventile still stands out.

Everything that was tier A on the full data reproduces on passages it was not measured on

Passages were split 50/50 at random and the full primary grid — five estimators, two variants, Pearson and Spearman, measured ESS and bootstrap CIs — recomputed on each half. The 36 cell correlations agree at r = +0.950 (+0.948 on ranks). All 13 tier-A cells have the same sign and a confidence interval excluding zero in both halves. The average gap between halves is 0.0133; if the two halves were measuring the same correlation with sampling noise only, it would be about 0.0131. The 4 cells that change sign (Qwen/mmlu, ERNIE/mmlu, Liquid/race, Liquid/structured-wikipedia) all sit within ±0.038 on both halves.

Reading the tier counts. Only 6 and 7 cells reach tier A on a single half. That is expected, not a loss: a half has half the effective sample, so tier A on a half (ARF ≥ 20 there) needs ARF ≥ 40 on the full data. 6 of the 13 have it. The experiment's own summary says all 13 tier-A designations are confirmed; more precisely, all 13 replicate in sign and significance, and the per-half tiers are what their full-data margins predict.

8. Difficulty control from both sides

9/13
tier-A cells surviving both controls
+0.034 to +0.089
Qwen tier-A, controlling the small model's loss
1e-12
largest gap, v10.5 reconstruction vs measurement
2 / 2
Gemma tier-A cells: scale-specific / easy-token

Because IG = CEsmall − CEbig, controlling one model's loss turns the question into whether HC predicts the other model's loss beyond it, and a pure difficulty marker can pass either one-sided test (v10.5 showed this by simulation). A cell is credited with a scale-specific association only if it survives both: under each control the partial keeps the raw sign, sits outside the cell's measured floor, and its sign-consistency score across the ten configurations is at least 0.7 — the tier-B threshold, which means at least 9 of 10 agree. The control on the mean of the two losses is reported alongside as the symmetric middle ground.

The measurement confirms the reconstruction exactly

v10.5 solved r(HC, IG | CEsmall) from four summary correlations for the GMM/standard configuration. Measured on tokens, it agrees to 1e-12 in magnitude in all 36 cells and in sign in all 24 cells where the reconstruction had one plausible root. Where it had two, the measured value was one of them. The reconstruction did its job; what changes now is that the control runs on all ten configurations, not one.

Qwen: scale-specific in all four tier-A benchmarks

Controlling the small model's loss, Qwen's correlation stays positive and outside the floor in competition_math (+0.034), lambada (+0.085), fineweb-edu (+0.089) and race (+0.046), with all ten configurations positive in each. Controlling the mean of the two losses it keeps 98%–118%. Within deciles of the small model's loss, r(HC, IG) is positive in 10 of 10 for lambada, fineweb-edu and race. Under the rule written in v10.5, ‘where scale helps’ is tier A for Qwen.

competition_math is the narrow case. Only 34% of its raw correlation survives the small-model control, the rank version of that partial is -0.011, and within small-model deciles 1–8 there is no relationship at all. It all sits in the hardest tenth for the small model (mean loss 6.8 nats), where r = +0.286 and the top 10% of HC has 2.9 nats more IG than the rest. Among the tokens the small model gets badly wrong, HC picks out the ones the large model gets right. That is ‘where scale helps’ in its sharpest form, but it is a statement about roughly a tenth of the tokens, which is why ranks and the middle-decile curve (0.09 → 0.05) do not see it.

Figure 17 — The 13 tier-A cells under each difficulty control, measured

Amber is the control v10.5 had to reconstruct. Qwen's four keep it; Gemma's pg19 and fineweb-edu, ERNIE's pg19 lose it.

Figure 18 — Qwen: HC–IG correlation within each decile of small-model difficulty

lambada, fineweb-edu and race stay positive throughout. competition_math is flat until the last decile, where the small model fails.

Gemma: two different things share one sign

In competition_math and race, Gemma's negative association survives both controls (-0.108 and -0.039 under CEsmall, every configuration negative) and stays negative within most small-model deciles (positive in only 2 and 2 of 10). There, among tokens equally hard for the small model, high HC marks tokens the large model does worse on: a scale-specific inversion.

In pg19 and fineweb-edu it does not survive. pg19 falls to -0.014, inside its ±0.015 floor; fineweb-edu to -0.012, with the ten configurations split on sign. Within small-model deciles the correlation is positive in 9 and 10 of 10. Gemma's HC is negative against both losses, so in these two benchmarks the negative IG correlation comes from HC flagging tokens that are easy for both models; once that is held fixed, what remains points the same way as Qwen's.

The v10.5 rule asked for three or more Gemma cells inside the floor before restating Gemma's whole result as easy-token marking. One is, so the rule is not met, and the split is the more accurate description anyway. v10.5's Gemma statement, made from the GMM/standard reconstruction alone, called race sign-ambiguous; on the full grid it is clear.

Figure 19 — Gemma: HC–IG correlation within each decile of small-model difficulty

competition_math falls steadily with small-model difficulty and race stays slightly negative; pg19 and fineweb-edu sit at or above zero once small-model difficulty is held fixed. Within-decile correlations are small except in competition_math.

ERNIE and Liquid

ERNIE/lambada is unresolved: strongly negative under the small-model control (-0.067) but weak and split across configurations under the large-model one (-0.019). v10.5 called it a difficulty artifact from the large-model side alone; that was premature. ERNIE/pg19 is the mirror image: strong under the large-model control, +0.006 under the small-model one, so its positive association is shared difficulty. Liquid's three tier-A cells survive both, including competition_math, which v10.5 had marked as partly difficulty from the large-model side.

For Qwen's competition_math and lambada (where IG surges in the top HC ventile) and fineweb-edu (where it falls), the experiment compared the top ventile with the 75th–90th percentile band: token class, the most frequent token strings, position in the passage, and routing statistics, and it recomputed the binned curve within each major class. GMM/standard; routing statistics, like all HC in the series, from the last MoE layer.

The surge is not a token-class artifact at the level of word, symbol and punctuation

In lambada, words are 80% of the top ventile (reference 87%), and the surge is the same within words (+0.82) and within punctuation (+0.83). In competition_math no class exceeds 54%; the surge holds within words (+1.27) and math symbols (+0.74). The experiment's punctuation figure (-2.68) is misleading: within punctuation's own HC ventiles, IG peaks at 2.9 and 4.0 nats in ventiles 16–17 and drops in the last one, so the surge is there, one step earlier. By the v10.5 rule, that made the surge a routing property; section 10 shows the classes were too coarse to support it.

Figure 20 — Token classes in the top HC ventile against the reference band

Qwen. competition_math and fineweb-edu gain punctuation at the top; fineweb-edu loses words and numbers.

But the class labels are too coarse to settle it

The most frequent token strings tell a more specific story. In lambada's top ventile they are ‘·'’ (366), ‘·n’ (228), ‘·j’ (49), ‘·d’ (23), ‘·h’ (21), ‘·g’ (20) — word-initial fragments and apostrophes, the pieces a tokenizer produces for rare words and names. The ten most frequent strings make up 38% of the ventile. In competition_math they are ‘,’ (164), ‘real’ (148), ‘);\n\n’ (108), ‘?\n’ (105), ‘·{\n\n’ (102), ‘;\n’ (98) — code punctuation and keywords such as ‘real’, which most likely come from the Asymptote diagram code embedded in many MATH problems (25% of the ventile in ten strings). All of these count as ‘word’ or ‘punctuation’ in the class test, so the surge surviving within classes does not show it survives within token types. The decisive version compares the same token string inside and outside the top HC ventile.

fineweb-edu's fall at the top is token composition

v10 found that in fineweb-edu IG falls in the top HC ventile and left the reason open. The top ventile is 35% punctuation (reference 19%) and only 35% words (reference 54%), led by line breaks and full stops. Punctuation carries little IG, and within each class IG does not fall at the top: words +0.16, punctuation +0.07, the rest within ±0.05. The experiment's summary calls this a drop ‘pervasive across all token categories’; its own within-class numbers say the opposite. The overall fall comes from which tokens reach the top, not from what happens to tokens of a given kind.

Figure 21 — fineweb-edu: mean IG across HC ventiles, within each class

Words sit high and keep rising; punctuation and numbers sit low and flat. A top ventile rich in punctuation therefore has lower mean IG overall.

Routing and position. Top-ventile tokens use a narrower set of experts (participation ratio 36 against 48 in competition_math, 17 against 26 in lambada) and different ones: the top-20 experts overlap with the reference band's by 0.14 and 0.08 (Jaccard), against 0.43 in fineweb-edu. Some of the concentration is built into HC, which is high when a few experts' p-values are extreme. Position matters little; lambada's top ventile is slightly over-represented in the last tenth of the passage (13% against 8%), where LAMBADA's target word sits.

Provenance. The experiment's metadata names the model ‘Qwen-2.5-32B’ and layer 47. Qwen-2.5-32B is a dense model; the routing statistics here use expert indices up to 127, which matches Qwen3-30B-A3B's 128 experts and 48 layers, of which layer 47 is the last — the layer every HC value in the series comes from. So the model name is most likely a label slip; the layer is the expected one.

For each token string that occurs often enough both in the top HC ventile and in the 75th–90th percentile band, the experiment took the difference in mean IG between the two, and pooled those differences with fixed-effects weights. That asks whether a given token, when its HC is in the top 5%, shows more IG than the same token slightly lower down. Separately it demeaned HC and IG within each string and recomputed the correlation, which asks whether the graded relationship holds among occurrences of the same token.

Within the same token, little of the surge remains

competition_math. Eighteen strings qualify, covering 25% of the top ventile. Their pooled within-string difference is +0.123 nats against a raw surge of 0.937: 13%, CI -0.038 to +0.257. Weighting or comparing differently gives 13%–30%, never near the 50% the rule asks for a routing property. Under the rule's primary contrast it is below 25%: the surge is mostly the result of particular tokens — code punctuation, ‘Solution’, ‘real’, ‘if’ — landing in the top ventile.

lambada. Only 2 strings qualify (‘ '’ and ‘ n’), and they almost never appear in the reference band (0.4% of it). 74% of the top ventile is strings that occur more often there than in the whole rest of the corpus. The contrast against the reference band (+0.61, CI -0.41 to +1.76) is too noisy to read; against the rest of the corpus the same two strings keep 16% of the surge. In lambada, high HC largely is the token type: those pieces — most likely the tokenizer's split of contractions and rare words — always route anomalously, and the large model is much better at what follows them.

By the v11 rule, both surges are about which tokens reach the top, and v10's tier-A shape finding is restated accordingly. The experiment's summary reaches the same label for lambada, but with a rationale that calls 68% ‘below 25%’; the label rests on the token exclusivity, not on that number.

The graded correlation does survive within token strings

Demeaning HC and IG within each token string removes everything that differs between token types. What is left is whether, for a given token, higher HC goes with higher IG. In competition_math the correlation falls from +0.144 to +0.070 (CI +0.051 to +0.087): about half is between token types, half within. In lambada it keeps +0.091 of +0.123, in fineweb-edu all of it (+0.061), and Gemma's competition_math inversion is unchanged (-0.070).

So two things separate cleanly. The surge — the sharp jump in the top 5% of HC — is mostly token identity. The correlation, which is what the tier-A claims are about, is mostly not. The ‘where scale helps’ claim for Qwen stands; what changes is the description of its shape.

Figure 22 — The correlation with and without between-token differences

GMM, standard. Within-string correlation keeps half of competition_math's and most or all of the others'.

fineweb-edu and the Gemma control. fineweb-edu's top-of-HC fall is mostly composition, as v11 found, but not entirely: within the same string the top ventile still sits 0.098 nats lower (CI -0.145 to -0.033), about 44% of the fall. Gemma's competition_math decline survives within strings (-0.041, CI -0.066 to -0.015, 77% retained), so Gemma's scale-specific inversion there is not a token-type effect.

Coverage. Only strings frequent in both groups can be tested, so the within-string surge describes 25% of competition_math's top ventile and 30% of lambada's. The rest is rarer strings, where the test has nothing to compare. If anything that strengthens the token-type reading: the rarer the string, the less it can be explained by HC varying within it. One configuration (GMM, standard).

The experiment demeaned HC, CEbig, CEsmall and IG within each token string (strings with fewer than five occurrences pooled into one group) and recomputed both partial correlations on all 360 configurations. Everything that differs between token types is removed; what remains asks whether, for a given token, the occurrences with higher HC are the ones where the large model's advantage exceeds what either model's loss predicts.

Qwen: the scale-specific signal holds token by token

All four tier-A cells survive both controls within strings. Holding the small model's loss fixed: competition_math +0.027, lambada +0.035, fineweb-edu +0.073, race +0.069; holding the large model's: competition_math +0.067, lambada +0.144, fineweb-edu +0.062, race +0.070. Every one of the ten configurations is positive in every cell, and the smallest single-configuration lower CI bound is +0.006. By the v12 rule, ‘where scale helps’ is a property of how a given token is routed, and that line joins the claim at tier A.

How much survives differs by benchmark. In fineweb-edu and race the within-string partial is close to or above the raw one (82% and 150%): the signal there never depended on token identity. In competition_math it keeps 78% and in lambada 41%. Those are the surge benchmarks, where part of the scale-specific signal is about which tokens reach the top, consistent with v12.

Figure 24 — The 13 tier-A cells: the two difficulty controls within token strings

Grey is the v11 small-model control on raw values; amber the same control within strings; blue the large-model control within strings. Qwen's four keep both. Gemma/competition_math's amber bar shrinks to near the floor.

Gemma, ERNIE and Liquid within strings

Gemma. race survives both controls within strings (-0.031, every configuration negative). competition_math does not: its small-model partial falls from -0.108 to -0.018 with the configurations split, so its scale-specific inversion is about which kinds of token appear, not how a given token is routed. pg19 goes the other way, from inside the floor on raw values to -0.021 within strings (9 of 10 configurations negative). fineweb-edu stays large-model-only. Gemma's scale-specific inversion is therefore solid only in race.

ERNIE/lambada stays split: within strings the large-model control turns positive (+0.034) while the small-model control stays strongly negative. ERNIE/pg19 remains shared difficulty. Liquid: competition_math and lambada survive both within strings; tinystories loses the large-model side (+0.013).

The nulls disagree about which tokens are most anomalous

For competition_math, the experiment listed the top HC ventile under each of the ten configurations. The sets barely overlap across estimators: against GMM/standard, Jaccard 0.13–0.66; KDE's top ventile shares 13% of its tokens with GMM's. Under GMM and StudentT the top is code punctuation and ‘real’; under JohnsonSU it is LaTeX backslashes; under KDE it is ‘ the’, ‘Solution’, ‘ is’. The correlation-level results agree across estimators because they are driven by the bulk of tokens; the identity of the extreme tail is not robust to the null.

Across configurations the surge follows the share of code tokens in the top ventile: ρ = 0.806 with the top-bin jump, just above the pre-registered 0.8, so the estimator caveat on competition_math's surge is lifted. It is a narrow pass: the other surge measure gives 0.71, and dropping StudentTSkewed gives 0.62. Word and punctuation shares do not track the surge at all.

14. Out of domain: two unseen benchmarks

Two benchmarks the series had never used were chosen before looking: mbpp, short Python programming problems, and dialogsum, dialogues with summaries. The full pipeline ran for Qwen and Gemma on each — raw correlation, Spearman, both difficulty controls on raw values and within token strings, five estimators, two variants. The prediction, written in v13: Qwen positive and outside the floor under both controls within strings; Gemma negative or null.

Qwen: one narrow pass, one reversal, and a negative raw sign on both

dialogsum. Within token strings both controls are positive: | CEbig +0.100 (all ten configurations) and | CEsmall +0.012 (nine of ten; mean CI +0.005 to +0.019). That meets the prediction, with the floor set from dialogsum's own implied ESS (0.0067). It is small — about half of what Qwen's weakest studied tier-A cell shows within strings — and it sits on top of a negative raw correlation (-0.035; Spearman -0.063). Within token strings the association is positive; between token types it is strongly negative and wins overall.

mbpp. Raw r is -0.043. Within strings the large-model control is weakly positive (+0.027, eight of ten configurations positive) and the small-model control is negative (-0.028): holding the small model's loss fixed, high-HC occurrences of a token are ones the large model handles worse. Eight configurations agree; StudentTSkewed, both variants, goes the other way.

In all nine studied benchmarks Qwen's raw correlation was positive. On both new ones it is negative. Whatever makes HC track where Qwen's scale helps, it is not a property of Qwen's routing that holds regardless of the text.

Figure 26 — Unseen benchmarks: raw and within-string correlations

Means of ten configurations. The prediction concerned the blue and amber bars: positive for Qwen, negative or null for Gemma.

Figure 27 — Qwen, unseen benchmarks: the scale-specific part under each configuration

mbpp is negative except under StudentTSkewed; dialogsum is positive except under GMM/standard.

Gemma: the raw inversion carries over; the scale-specific part does not behave as predicted

Gemma's raw correlation is negative on both benchmarks in every configuration (mbpp -0.056, dialogsum -0.086), the first out-of-domain support for the series' Gemma result. Within strings, mbpp is negative under both controls (-0.118 and -0.029, the latter in eight of ten configurations). dialogsum's small-model control is positive (+0.063, all ten configurations): among occurrences of the same token with the same small-model loss, high HC marks ones where Gemma's large model does better. That is the prediction failing for Gemma on dialogsum, and it points the same way as Qwen there.

Reading the pre-registered rule

The rule said a pass on a new benchmark confirms the claim out of domain, and a miss on all of them restricts it to the studied benchmarks. dialogsum passes, so the letter says ‘confirmed’. The rule did not anticipate a significant result in the opposite direction on the other benchmark, and the v9 and v10.5 cycles both showed what happens when a rule has a gap: the honest course is to state the letter and then say what the evidence supports. Here that is narrower than the letter. The Qwen claim stays tier A on the nine studied benchmarks; out of domain it is mixed (B), and the next experiment widens the sample of unseen text rather than leaning on one pass.

v12: the two-sided control across partners

The scale-specific part shrinks faster than the association as the gap closes

With the large model fixed, r(HC, IG | CEsmall) averages +0.041 with the 0.6B partner, +0.026 with 1.7B and +0.009 with 4B, falling by 79% while the raw correlation falls by 56%. Its share of the raw correlation goes 64% → 51% → 31%. The ordering is strict in 8 of 9 benchmarks. Under the v11 rule, the compute gap scales the scale-specific signal, and a signal that measures where scale helps should do exactly that.

It is uneven. In the surge benchmarks the scale-specific part collapses: competition_math +0.066 → +0.007, structured-wikipedia +0.034 → +0.002, and lambada reverses to -0.033 with the 4B partner. In fineweb-edu, race and pg19 it falls much less and stays clearly positive (+0.076 → +0.064, +0.036 → +0.023, +0.055 → +0.032). That is consistent with the token-type reading: where the signal rides on a few token types the large model handles far better than a 0.6B model, a 4B partner closes that gap; where it is spread through the body of HC, it survives even when the small partner has more active parameters than the large one, which still has about seven times more parameters in total.

Figure 32 — The scale-specific part of Qwen's association, by partner

The first three (blue, teal, purple) are the surge benchmarks; their scale-specific part collapses or reverses. The last three fall much less. GMM, standard.

The experiment's summary gives the shares as -18.6%, 52.8% and -413.6%. Those are averages of per-benchmark ratios, several with a raw correlation near zero in the denominator; the ratio of the family means is the meaningful number.

v13: the lambada reversal with the 4B partner

Not a token-type effect, and not yet explained

With the 4B partner, lambada's scale-specific part is -0.033 (CI -0.044 to -0.021): holding the 4B model's loss fixed, high-HC tokens are ones where the 4B model does better than Qwen3-30B-A3B. The two near-exclusive strings do not carry it: without ‘ '’ and ‘ n’ the partial is -0.056, and within token strings -0.047 (CI -0.059 to -0.033). By the v12 rule it is an open anomaly.

What the per-string numbers do show is how the surge tokens lose their special status as the partner grows. IG on ‘ '’ falls from 2.31 to 0.70 nats and on ‘ n’ from 2.81 to 0.76, while other top-ventile tokens fall from 1.26 to 0.89: with the 4B partner the near-exclusive strings carry less IG than the rest of the top ventile. The experiment's summary attributes the reversal to the 4B model having more active parameters than the large model's 3.3B. That would predict reversals in other benchmarks with the same partner, and fineweb-edu, race and pg19 keep positive scale-specific parts there (+0.064, +0.023, +0.032). It stays a hypothesis.

17. The IG-quantile slices (retired in v8)

Q50–Q95 keep tokens whose IG is at or above its Nth percentile. On identical tokens, that selection raised the HC–IG correlation in 27 of 27 experiment-3 cases (median ×1.9) and turned tinystories' +0.001 into +0.121. Experiment 1 showed the IG-selected values reproduce on held-out passages (r = +0.97), which is stability, not evidence of prediction. Nothing in this report uses them.

What is specific to Gemma

Gemma's inversion is the most robust single pattern in the study: negative under all five estimators and both GLM versions, on ranks, linear through HC's whole range, and with the compute gap ruled out. CheckStatusResult
Grid completeness & numeric sanitydone432/432 cells, 0 duplicates, 0 unparsed columns. Avg_Inverse_Min_P still overflows (8.1e298) — descriptive only. The 26_08_30 full-network correlations and the 26_09_03 max_20pct correlations are identical in 1296/1296 rows (max difference 1e-16), so the two drops are joined exactly.
Monte-Carlo null reproductiondoneσ = 0.009866, crit_05 = 0.01934 reproduces — but it was computed at n = 10,000, which is the simulation size, not the sample size. Real n runs 12,314–477,782 (median 51,100). The iid floor is retired in favour of the measured one.
Empirical (Efron) nulldoneσ0 = 6.0 at measured ESS, 8.4 at true nominal n, 10.9 at the old n = 10,000 assumption. The residual is between-family heterogeneity, not a broken yardstick.
Block-bootstrap nulldonePassage-level bootstrap (1,000 resamples) on the full token set with the series' own statistic: 299/360 IG configurations exclude 0. Median deflation 2.61×. Both new experiments reuse the same passage bootstrap, so their CIs and grades are on the same footing.
Multiplicity / effective test countdone1.15 of 10 configurations per cell (mean pairwise r = 0.93); 360 configurations ≈ 41 independent tests.
BH false discovery ratedone292 of 360 full-network IG configurations at q < 0.05 on ESS-honest z. Permutation p-values are not used: 267/360 sit at the 1e-4 floor.
Autocorrelation robustness (ARF)doneGraded at each cell's own measured ESS. 14 of 36 full-network IG cells clear ARF ≥ 20 beyond their measured ESS.
Estimator consistencydoneResolved by a pre-registered decision. GLM removed from the primary grid (experiment 2): spread 0.0134 against the 0.0128 floor, down from 0.0252 with GLM; all original tier-A cells keep tier A and every family keeps its sign. Cause identified in the code: the Lindsey GLM extrapolates a Laplace tail, so extreme routing logits get far larger p-values. Residual per family: Qwen 0.0192, ERNIE 0.0179, Gemma 0.0296, Liquid 0.0149. Gemma's magnitudes still depend on the estimator; its signs do not. v10: a Gaussian-decay GLM removes the Laplace offset but scatters instead — inside the five-estimator envelope in 39% of cells, where each of the five lands inside the other four's in 50%–72%. The Lindsey GLM is dropped permanently.
HC variant consistencydonePass: spread 0.0038, inside the 0.0128 floor.
Control retention (Fisher, p_min)doneOn the five-estimator grid. Qwen retains 69% under Fisher and 82% under pmin; Gemma 45% and 76%. Across the 24 cells more than twice the floor, median retention is 56% (Fisher) and 77% (pmin). ERNIE and Liquid have no raw effect to retain.
Layer-subset selectiondoneSuperseded by a definition error. The ‘Q50–Q95 layer subsets’ are tokens whose Intelligence Gain is above its 50th–95th percentile (verified in the pipeline code and by an exact reproduction). Selecting on the outcome cannot support a claim that HC predicts it, so the selection question is moot: the primary slice is reset to the full token set.
Effect size (decile lift)doneFormula lift reported for every headline cell. E3 measured the lift empirically on the full token set; across 21 Qwen cells with |r| > 0.02 the empirical lift is 1.50× the 1.755·r formula (range -0.65–2.54). New in v9: the rank results explain why — Qwen's association is concentrated in the upper part of HC's range, which lifts the top decile above what a linear relationship predicts.
Rank / heavy-tail robustnessdoneRun for the first time (experiment 1, on all 36 cells). 1%-winsorised Pearson keeps 0.91–1.05 of r in every tier-A cell, so a handful of extreme tokens is not the story. Spearman keeps a median 0.86; one tier-A cell (ERNIE/fineweb-edu, promoted by the GLM drop) falls below half and is demoted by the pre-registered rule. Qwen's ratio (0.71) is well below the other families'. v10: ties ruled out as the cause — the largest block of identical HC values is a median 0.19% of tokens (max 4.4%), and tie share is unrelated to the rank ratio (ρ = +0.09).
Sign-convention invariantdonePass everywhere: E1 0/11, E3 0/8, 26_09_03 max_20pct 0/35 testable rows inconsistent.
Statistic definition auditdoneThree corrections. (1) ‘Q75’ keeps 25.0% of tokens, chosen by IG ≥ its 75th percentile — selection on the outcome, not upper layers. (2) Max_Per_Row is max_20pct (identical in 432/432 cells). (3) The 26_08_30 drop is the full corpus, not a 10,000-token subsample.
Shape of the HC–IG relationshipdoneNew (v10). 20 HC bins per cell, covariance split by HC quartile (GMM/standard). The pre-registered threshold condition (top quartile > 70% of covariance, lower three quartiles inside the floor) holds in one Qwen tier-A cell, competition_math (78%, lower-quartile r +0.010); lambada is tail-amplified (77%) with a correlated body; fineweb-edu and pg19 fall in the top bin. Gemma's covariance is spread evenly (median top-quartile share 53%). Neither rule branch applies to Qwen as a whole, so the Pearson grades stand.
Out-of-sample replicationdonev10.5, random passage split, full primary grid. Halves correlate +0.950 across 36 cells (+0.948 on ranks); all 13 tier-A cells keep their sign with a CI excluding zero in both halves; half-to-half differences average 0.0133, the size sampling noise predicts (0.0131). Tier A per half 6 and 7 — what halving the sample predicts, since 6 cells have ARF ≥ 40. Both Qwen surges reproduce. (v8's E1 replicated the retired IG-selected slice.)
Difficulty-gap confounddonev10.5, token level. Partialling CEbig keeps ≥ 60% of r(HC, IG) in 11 of 13 tier-A cells, all of Qwen's and Gemma's; it fails in ERNIE/lambada (19%), Liquid/competition_math (38%). Within CEbig deciles, the top-HC-decile IG lift is positive in 10 of 10 for Qwen competition_math and lambada. Caveat: this partial equals r(HC, CEsmall | CEbig), and a noisy difficulty proxy leaves it positive even if HC tracked difficulty alone; see the next row.
Two-sided difficulty controldonev11, measured on tokens, full primary grid. r(HC, IG | CEsmall) and | mean CE for all 360 configurations. 9 of 13 tier-A cells survive both one-sided controls (sign kept, outside the floor, sign-consistency score ≥ 0.7, i.e. at least 9 of 10 configurations agreeing), including all four of Qwen's. The v10.5 reconstruction matches the measurement to 1e-12 in magnitude in all 36 cells and in sign in all 24 it called determined.
Top-ventile token compositiondoneNew (v11). Token class, position and expert use for Qwen's top HC ventile in competition_math, lambada and fineweb-edu. The surge holds within the major syntactic classes in competition_math and lambada; the fineweb-edu fall at the top is a composition effect. The class taxonomy is coarse: the ten most frequent token strings make up 38% of lambada's top ventile.
Within-token-type testdoneNew (v12). Fixed-effects contrast of the same string in the top HC ventile against the 75th–90th band. competition_math keeps 13% of its surge (CI -0.04 to +0.26); lambada has only 2 testable strings, because 74% of its top-ventile tokens are strings that occur more often there than everywhere else combined. The graded correlation survives within strings: +0.070 of +0.144 in competition_math, +0.091 of +0.123 in lambada.
Estimator robustness of shape and stratadoneNew (v12). Eight tier-A cells × ten configurations. Qwen's lambada surge and all small-model strata for lambada, fineweb-edu and race hold everywhere. competition_math's surge does not: top-bin jump -0.04 to +1.42, absent under JohnsonSU and KDE. Gemma's pg19 and fineweb-edu strata signs depend on the configuration.
Two-sided control across compute ratiosdoneNew (v12). Qwen with the 0.6B, 1.7B and 4B partners (GMM/standard). Family mean r(HC, IG | CEsmall) +0.041 → +0.026 → +0.009, falling faster than the raw correlation (share 64% → 31%).
Two-sided control within token stringsdoneNew (v13). HC, both losses and IG demeaned within each token string; both partials on all 360 configurations. All four Qwen tier-A cells survive both controls (r(HC, IG | CEsmall) within strings +0.027 to +0.073, every configuration positive). 8 of 13 tier-A cells survive both within strings.
Null dependence of the top-ventile tokensdoneNew (v13). competition_math, ten configurations. Top-ventile token sets overlap with GMM/standard's by Jaccard 0.13–0.66. The surge tracks the share of code tokens (ρ = 0.81, against a pre-registered 0.8).
Lambada reversal decompositiondoneNew (v13). Persists without the two near-exclusive strings (-0.056) and within token strings (-0.047, CI excluding zero). Not a token-type effect; unexplained.
Out-of-domain confirmationdoneNew (v14). mbpp (code) and dialogsum (dialogue), Qwen and Gemma, ten configurations. Raw r(HC, IG) for Qwen is negative on both (-0.043, -0.035). Within strings the scale-specific part is +0.012 on dialogsum, outside its floor, and -0.028 on mbpp, the opposite sign. No measured ESS or token counts in the drop; floors are implied by the bootstrap CI widths.
Layer provenancedoneStated in v14.1. All of them come from the last MoE layer of each large model, and only from it. Consistent with every drop: v8 found no layer axis in any file, and the top-ventile drop names layer 47 of Qwen3-30B-A3B, its last. Earlier reports did not say so; no number changes.

The same register as section 1.

24. Assessment

Holds up

  • On the nine studied benchmarks, Qwen's ‘where scale helps’ holds at every level tested: both difficulty controls, within token strings, every configuration, held-out halves, across compute ratios.
  • Gemma's raw inversion generalises: negative on both unseen benchmarks, every configuration.
  • HC tracks token difficulty in all four families; 31 and 28 of 36 cells outside the floor.
  • The series' method: pre-registered rules, exact reconstruction checks, and verdicts recomputed from source tables.

Not yet established

  • Out of domain, Qwen's raw sign reverses on both new benchmarks; the within-string pass on dialogsum is narrow.
  • One layer. Everything is last-MoE-layer routing; no earlier layer, and no simpler last-layer baseline, has been compared.
  • The unseen-benchmark drop lacks measured ESS, token counts and raw CIs; floors are inferred.
  • Gemma's scale-specific part is positive on dialogsum, against prediction; its cause is open.
  • Only two unseen benchmarks, both unusual in format (code; dialogue with speaker tags).
  • The extreme tail is null-dependent, and the lambada 4B reversal is unexplained.

Open

  • Is the out-of-domain reversal about format tokens (speaker tags, code indentation) that sit between token types?
  • How many unseen benchmarks of ordinary prose behave like the studied nine?
  • Is Gemma/race's inversion carried by the shared expert?
  • Does a larger partner reverse other benchmarks too?

25. Next experiments

What happened to v13's list

v13 experimentStatusOutcome
Confirmatory run on unseen benchmarks (P0)DoneRule met by the letter (dialogsum); mbpp reverses; raw sign negative on both. Claim scoped to the studied benchmarks.
Shared-expert ablation in Gemma's large model (P1)Not runCarried; design simplified in v14.1 (HC is last-layer).
A larger partner for the active-compute hypothesis (P1)Not runCarried, now P2.
Lambada's top ventile under every null (P2)Not runCarried.

Proposed

Complete the unseen-benchmark drop

P0 · an hour, existing outputs
Question
dialogsum's pass depends on a floor inferred from bootstrap widths, and the Gemma inputs were flagged as not ready minutes before the results were written.
Design
Add token counts, passage counts and measured ESS (the 26_09_03 ACF method) for all four cells; raw-level bootstrap CIs; confirm the Gemma loss-difference files were complete when the analysis ran, and rerun if not.
Statistic
Measured floor per cell; dialogsum's within-string r(HC, IG | CEsmall) against it.
Decision rule
If dialogsum stays outside its measured floor with at least 9 of 10 configurations positive, the letter of the v13 rule stands. If it falls inside, the out-of-domain result is restated as no pass on either benchmark.

Widen the unseen sample

P0 · ~1–2 days, forward passes on new text
Question
Two unusual benchmarks cannot say whether the Qwen result is domain-general with exceptions or specific to the studied kinds of text.
Design
Four more benchmarks fixed before looking, chosen to span ordinary prose as well as structured text: for example news, scientific abstracts, a second code set, and open-ended chat. Same pipeline, both families, with measured ESS.
Statistic
Raw r(HC, IG) and the within-string partials per benchmark, against measured floors.
Decision rule
Prediction fixed now: Qwen positive and outside the floor under both controls within strings. If it holds on at least four of the six unseen benchmarks, the claim is restated as domain-general with named exceptions. If on two or fewer, it is restated as specific to the studied benchmark types, and the raw-sign reversal becomes a finding in its own right.

Last-layer baselines

P0 · a few hours, from the same forward passes
Question
HC is computed at the last MoE layer, the one feeding the output head. Does it add anything beyond simpler signals from the same layer?
Design
From the last MoE layer: router entropy, the maximum router probability, the top-1 minus top-2 logit gap, and the norm of the hidden state entering the layer. For Qwen's four tier-A cells and Gemma's race: r(HC, IG) partialled on each baseline and on all of them together, both difficulty controls, within token strings.
Statistic
Retention of the within-string scale-specific partial after the baselines are partialled out.
Decision rule
If at least half of Qwen's within-string r(HC, IG | CEsmall) survives all baselines in three or more of the four cells, HC carries information the simpler signals do not. If less than a quarter survives, the result is restated in terms of the baseline that absorbs it.

Layer sweep

P1 · ~1 day, existing forward passes if router logits were cached
Question
Where in the network does the relationship live? The question the retired Q-slices claimed to answer, asked properly.
Design
Compute HC from every MoE layer's router (same five estimators, two variants) for Qwen on its four tier-A benchmarks and Gemma on race. Raw r(HC, IG) and both difficulty controls per layer.
Statistic
r and the scale-specific partial as a function of layer depth.
Decision rule
If the scale-specific partial is outside the floor only in the last few layers, the finding is stated as a property of late routing. If it appears from the middle layers on, the claim widens to routing in general and the last-layer choice stops being a caveat.

What drives the negative raw sign out of domain

P1 · a few hours, existing token series
Question
On dialogsum the within-string association is positive but the raw one negative, so the between-token-type part is strongly negative. Which token types carry it?
Design
Decompose r(HC, IG) into between- and within-string parts for dialogsum and mbpp. Rank token strings by their contribution to the between part; check speaker tags (‘#Person1#:’), newlines and indentation explicitly. Recompute the raw correlation with those strings removed.
Statistic
Between-string contribution by token string; raw r with format tokens excluded.
Decision rule
If removing format tokens turns Qwen's raw r positive on dialogsum, the reversal is a formatting effect and the out-of-domain result is restated in those terms. If it stays negative, the reversal is about content.

Shared-expert ablation in Gemma's large model

P1 · ~half a day, existing models
Question
Is Gemma/race's scale-specific inversion carried by the always-active shared expert?
Design
Scale the last MoE layer's shared-expert output by 1, 0.5 and 0 and recompute CEbig on race and competition_math. Because HC comes from that layer's router, which in a standard MoE block reads the hidden state before the layer's expert outputs are added, HC is unchanged by construction: only CEbig moves, which isolates the shared expert's contribution to IG cleanly. As a second arm, ablate the shared experts of all layers, which does change last-layer routing, and recompute HC too.
Statistic
r(HC, IG | CEsmall) at each setting; the large model's mean CE at each setting.
Decision rule
If the race inversion shrinks by half or more at 0.5 while mean CE rises by less than 10%, the shared expert is implicated. If unchanged at 0, it is ruled out.

A larger partner and lambada's tokens under every null

P2 · ~half a day
Question
Carried from v13: does a Qwen3-8B partner reverse other benchmarks (the active-compute account of lambada's reversal), and are lambada's near-exclusive strings at the top under every null?
Design
Add Qwen3-8B as a fourth small partner and rerun the two-sided control on the nine studied benchmarks; list the top-ventile tokens of lambada under each of the ten configurations.
Statistic
r(HC, IG | CEsmall) per benchmark with the 8B partner; share of ‘ '’ and ‘ n’ in lambada's top ventile per configuration.
Decision rule
If three or more benchmarks turn negative with the 8B partner, the active-compute account is supported. If those two strings keep at least half their GMM share under every null, the lambada token-type description holds across nulls.
